title: Maybe the real reason we are all here…
author: InformationTop5376
selftext:
So I was thinking about it, maybe the real reason we are all here making stuff and having fun learning is to prepare for something greater, or to just say that we made a game (using AI or not). I’d really love for my first game to make money, but even if it’s a complete flop, I want to say I did it. And then move on to the next one with all the lessons learned chalked up as experience :)

I think I’ve had too much focus on being perfect (“perfect is the enemy of ‘good enough’”) trying to manage and appease a certain market segment that will never like what we do regardless of how good a game it is, all because of how we made it. I’ve landed on honest disclosure and the rest is out of our control.

Hope this resonates with someone. Let me know your thoughts.

comments.author: yungastronot
comments.body: Yeah I'm just having fun building. It's like legos on steroids. Maybe I'm addicted. I laugh at the anti-AI devs here that come to an AI sub to bash on people's personal projects. It's ok to just make stuff, even if it sucks

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: I get that addiction angle haha. Yeah, I’ve noticed that usually takes care of itself here since they usually get downvoted.

comments.author: necrohobo
comments.body:
Idk what you’re talking about. MY game would never flop on the first go around. Everyone is gonna love it because I’ve got the best idea!

\- all of us

We’ll all face the truth if we make it that far. I’m sure only a few will make it big, like all booms

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body:
Idk, I think some people need to learn the flop lesson first hand. Others simply don't have any commercial expectations. And still others learn from watching and understanding the landscape. 

Personally, I kill most of my own ideas after I prototype enough to see if there is fun. I run play tests with friends, family, and coworkers.  I typically don't ask "is this fun", I watch how they play, and see if there is enjoyment or curiosity to continue the loop. I don't need to release a full game to know it will flop, I already know if its crap just by playing it or watching others play.  Now, for many people, admitting that their game/idea is not good is the hard part.

replies.author: necrohobo
replies.body: I’ve been imagining my game for… decades. I can code all day, but was thinking “I’ll never be artistic”. Then AI came along.  So it really gives a chance to express ideas on an itch I’ve had for a long time. If it flops or succeeds then I’ll at least die in peace lol

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: for me, I would design all these games write down docs, bounce off ideas with chat gpt, then I realized how fast you can prototype the idea to realize if it's a good idea or not, traditional game dev it would take me probably 3-4 months to prototype an idea ( I'm slow ) but with ai assisted coding I could test it out in like a day to see if the idea I had in my head was fun or not

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Right now, I can’t discern if it’s “fun” or if it’s have rose colored glasses thinking it’s fun. But I guess that’s where playtest feedback comes in.

replies.author: barret232hxc
replies.body: oh noooo. are we all wearing ai glasses... I never thought about it like that.

comments.author: Little_Grimmy_Reap
comments.body: With the state of the industry it’s only natural people make games for themselves

comments.author: tfy-cape-town
comments.body:
Ive tried making games in the past. Maybe I was too ambitious. But I always end up giving up after a few months because of the mountain of work that is required as a solo dev. While having to work, raise a family etc.

AI (claude) is like having a team working on my game. With outcomes generated in minutes instead of hours or days.

A dream is to have a game on steam. Then more with each one getting better.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Yeah for sure. Same here. Working full time job, wife and two kids, and responsibilities on top of game dev. I like how I can iterate throughout the day on my phone, and then playtest on my staging server at night after kiddos are in bed. Been a nice cadence to work through. When I have a major update, I push it on up to itch.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
I'm certainly doing this to learn a whole lot about working with AI to develop software. The fact it is also fun to make games is a huge bonus. 

I've got to say though, I'm close to the stage where I'd like a couple of human partners to challenge ideas and give their expertise on art and UI.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Yeah I think that’s the next evolution for me as well. Trying to figure out when the right time is that I have enough expertise of game design to contribute something of value. Otherwise I’m just vibe coding.

comments.author: orbital_trace
comments.body: I've been building a game for two weeks. I thought the idea was really cool. But now I'm having troube finding a way to make it fun long term. Play testing takes a lot of time

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Definitely. Be sure to get other playtesters too either here or public itch page for your game.  That’s where you really learn if your game is fun or not.

comments.author: aeturnis-dev
comments.body:
Over the past year and a half we’ve iterated and prototyped 67 game ideas and projects and only 2 or 3 have gone beyond “That was a cool idea but…” and had serious time put into them. 

Most of the projects have been about learning what capabilities and limitations there are with AI development, and the biggest thing we’ve learned is research is invaluable. Have an idea? Research prior art, research cross-domain. Don’t churn ideas that have already solved answers. Terrain generation for example, why spend tokens, time and money trying to generate a from scratch process if there’s valuable lessons already out there for you to pull from?

Most of us here are hobbyists with a dream that is now actually tangible. AI is a force multiplier, not a magic button to make what you want. It still takes effort and time and understanding what you’re implementing.

Games have always had flops before AI. AI just makes more flops more available. The same for what people call “slop”. Humans have been capable of creating slop just fine without AI for decades, there’s just more of it now.

People get hung up on the aspect of that AI did it, it must be slop. No, it’s a tool and like any tool, if you use it appropriately it can do its job. They don’t care if you present evidence of your workflow, regression tests and all of that. They won’t see how you used and applied the tool as a force multiplier, only that you used AI.

Let them think that way, you won’t change their view no matter the evidence presented, and I say oh well. AI is still a very new and already very powerful thing, and it’s not going anywhere anytime soon and I feel we just happen to be at the frontier of where things are heading.

The landscape is still forming for AI and gaming.

comments.author: dgeisert
comments.body:
The best way to get good at making games is make more games and get more feedback.  The fastest way to do that is do game jams where you'll get feedback.  I'm hosting a jam starting on Friday if you want to join: [https://itch.io/jam/jamference-ai-game-jam-hack-2](https://itch.io/jam/jamference-ai-game-jam-hack-2)

The first one is going well and we are in the review period with lots of feedback and reviews for all the 32 games that were made last week.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Very cool. Does the game have to have been made in the first week? Or do you have to start the week the game jam starts?

replies.author: dgeisert
replies.body:
The games need to be made during the one week of the jam.  A new game each time.  Here is the list of games from the first jam: [https://itch.io/jam/jamference-ai-game-jam-hack-1/entries](https://itch.io/jam/jamference-ai-game-jam-hack-1/entries)

I'd recommend trying Neko Night Market and Laser Dot as two good examples that are quick to play.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Just joined. “Crafting” as the theme, I like it.
